cause: The evaluation recorder passed the provider response on with its content-encoding header after reading the decoded body, so the client decoded it a second time, failed, and the adapter resent requests that had succeeded (three identical requests per step in the pilot).
impact: The first pilot records were invalid and discarded; fixed before the baseline started, verified with 16 distinct request hashes in 16 calls.
lesson: An evaluation instrument is code under test: verify it on a pilot (request counts, hashes) before trusting a round.

cause: The v1.9.0 baseline takes hours and model runs import product code lazily, so implementation edits in the version worktree could leak into baseline tasks.
impact: The baseline runs from a detached checkout of tag v1.9.0 (.worktrees/eval-v190-baseline) with the harness copied in; four tasks already finished in the version worktree before any product change are kept; results go to the version worktree's local/agent-eval.
lesson: Run a long baseline from a pinned checkout so development can continue without contaminating it.

cause: The workflow adapter for iv.gmm and iv.weak_instruments passes the bound exog columns without an intercept, unlike the diagnostics and GLM-extension adapters; the pack oracle tests supply an explicit constant, so the consumer path was never compared with an oracle.
impact: Shipped since the IV-GMM pack was wired into workflows: Agent-run GMM estimates and weak-instrument partial F are wrong on data without a constant column (partial F 6223.5 instead of 170.6 in the baseline task); one baseline task concluded instruments were strong when the true first-stage F is about 4.
lesson: Oracle-test the path the consumer calls, not only the kernel; a kernel test with hand-built design matrices cannot see what the adapter leaves out.

cause: User asked (2026-10-18) to fix the IV workflow intercept failure now, with Stata oracle tests, while the baseline keeps running from the pinned v1.9.0 checkout.
impact: Commit 89357e5f: the IV adapter adds the intercept unless intercept is false or a bound column is constant; partial F, df, HC0 robust Wald F, 2SLS and two-step GMM coefficients match Stata 18 to 1e-9. Baseline comparisons list IV tasks separately because v1.9.0 ran with the bug.
lesson: Oracle-test the path the consumer calls, not only the kernel.

cause: OLS clustered standard errors need a cluster column, but model.genesis forbids entity_col for OLS and OLS model_options have no cluster field, so the Agent cannot cluster an OLS fit by classroom (baseline cluster_rct.specific, the STAR replication). The fix belongs in contracts/model, a protected path of this line reserved for the v1.9.2 inference kernel.
impact: cluster_rct and the STAR replication stay hard for the Agent in v1.9.1 (it can aggregate to cluster means instead); v1.9.2 adds OLS cluster-by-column with CR1/CR2 as part of the inference kernel.
lesson: A capability the Agent cannot name in a workflow does not exist for it, even when the UI form can do it.

cause: The orchestrator wrote each executed operation's whole result record as the model-visible text of its operation_result message; a Kaplan-Meier workflow result was ~450k characters (every curve point and censoring flag) and was resent on every later request and into compaction.
impact: v1.9.1 survival smoke runs reached 230k-580k prompt tokens per call (baseline profile: ~30k fixed); about 4 CNY of the smoke spend. Found from recorded tapes, no new calls.
lesson: Bound every server-written message the model reads, not only tool results; measure request anatomy per message from tapes after each smoke.

cause: Event 07234a72 estimated the cost of the unbounded operation results as about 4 CNY without computing it.
impact: Computed from the four smoke tapes at list prices (0.14/M miss, 0.0028/M hit, 0.28/M output USD): calls over 150k prompt tokens cost 0.32 USD (about 2.3 CNY) of the smoke's 0.42 USD total; the survival tasks alone 0.37 USD.
lesson: Compute spend figures from the tapes before recording them.

cause: The prior resource-regression acceptance did not certify the objective OLS 8-second target or all analysis/skill/browser evaluations. The default OLS synchronous contract also delays cancellation.

cause: Paid development replay exposed ambiguous primary evidence, wrong report refs, missing Agent AR reachability and repeated partial completion. A ConnectTimeout ended the last exchange without usage; the archived USD-times-8 estimate did not bound current CNY prices.

Known peak usage CNY 2.90194440 plus retained CNY 1.556964 reservation remains below 5. Paid round remains stopped. Offline exact-reference discovery passes the final standard group 1835/0; real efficacy and M5 remain unverified.

impact: Shared explicit native-IV AR and immutable report result refs now support six scripted Ask/Auto repair flows. Same-command correction preserves original budget, approvals and restart count. cause: Session lookups (get_entry, get_branch, append-once checks, transcript projection) re-read and re-parsed the whole JSONL log on every call, and navigation listed all operation records and re-read the event log once per message; cost grew with the square of the conversation length.
impact: Paid Ask round: 690-1115 s per task versus 118 s baseline median; offline replay of one real 3-step turn took 44.4 s. Offline scripted latency (37 ms per step) had not caught it because its fixture conversation was tiny.
lesson: Measure per-step server overhead on a real long conversation, not only on a small fixture.

cause: To profile a real session turn offline, Claude replaced the model adapter in agent_routes; after the M1 refactor adapters are created through runtime_adapter, so two profiling turns reached DeepSeek.
impact: Balance 43.27 -> 43.12 CNY (about 0.15 CNY) without user approval. Later profiling used headless_runtime_scope with a fake adapter and blocked httpx at the transport.
lesson: Any offline experiment blocks the network at the HTTP layer first, so a missed patch fails instead of billing.

cause: The completion gate required the Agent to copy exact run/artifact ids for the primary model, its companion diagnostics, alternative fits and a covering report, and its catalog scanned only the source run, so fits in branch runs were invisible.
impact: Paid Ask round: 0 of 4 tasks delivered, 5-8 nudges each, although the analyses were scientifically adequate (panel 0.514 vs truth 0.5). Fixed by server-side binding with the Agent keeping the primary choice; real-run effect still unmeasured.
lesson: A gate must ask the model only for decisions it alone can make; bookkeeping that follows from verified products belongs to the server.

cause: 1M-row import + OLS spent most time on per-value canonical encoding, repeated per-comparison group statistics and per-observation KDE evaluation; cancellation waited for one long uninterruptible fit call.
impact: Import + OLS 20.9 s -> about 12.9 s with byte-identical fingerprints and identical default test output; cancel-to-terminal 5.343 s -> 0.100-0.113 s. The 8 s target is still open: about 3.9 s remains in the protected econometrics/runner.py (per-value scalar conversion, row context), which needs the user's decision.
lesson: Profile the default path end to end and keep every optimization verifiable against stored golden output.

cause: The compact completion-evidence frame fingerprint hashed numpy column buffers; datetime64 and timedelta64 columns expose no buffer.
impact: Every panel, DID, IV, Cox or LMM fit on a frame with a date column failed since bc5f0990. Not caught because no completion test frame had a date column and the lineage guard lacked an iv.ar_confidence case.
lesson: Fingerprint code must be tested on every column dtype the importer produces, including dates.

cause: User approved (2026-10-21) changing protected econometrics/runner.py to split it and improve performance.
impact: runner.py split into ols_contract, ols_covariance and panel_iv; runner keeps run_ols, DID and the monkeypatched HONEST_* constants and re-exports moved names. Behaviour-preserving: 1756 econometrics tests, 1939 agent tests, 1M-row OLS result files byte-identical.
lesson: Before moving module-level constants, find every test that monkeypatches them and keep their readers in the patched module.

cause: tool_receipts.read re-read and strictly parsed the whole session log and then parsed it again via get_branch, about three times per tool call.
impact: Each tool step cost 0.33-0.69 s of Workbench time on recorded 8 MB sessions, growing with session length; after reading receipts from the shared log index it is 0.06-0.21 s (offline replay, network blocked).
lesson: Any durable-log reader on the per-step path must use the shared incremental index, never a whole-file parse.

cause: I treated the tape's 'at' field as the response end time; recorder.py writes the request start time.
impact: I told the user per-step non-model overhead was 1.5-2 s (5x the target) and that removing duplicate proposal content would save 20-30% of new tokens; the correct figures were about 0.5 s per step and 2-4% of context. Both were corrected before any code decision depended on them.
lesson: Read the writer of a recorded field before computing from it, and measure a proposed saving on recorded data before quoting it.

cause: User asked (2026-10-21/22) to split the large modules, improve the architecture and performance.
impact: Split agent/core.py, statistical_tests.py, engine/stages/estimation.py, http/notebook_routes.py, context_tools_support/registration.py (static tool descriptors to tool_specs.py) and agent/operations.py, behaviour-preserving: statements moved verbatim, layers import downward, patched names stay where tests patch them, 1M-row OLS and statistical-test outputs byte-identical, all 44 tool descriptors byte-identical, full suite 9502 passed (only failures: the 10 GB free-disk guard at 8.9 GB free). My statement-moving tool dropped comments between statements in the earlier data_operations split; found by a comment-line diff and restored (886366c1).
lesson: A mechanical split is verified by a comment-line diff against the pre-split file as well as by tests and byte comparisons.

cause: The LLM client discarded DeepSeek reasoning_content although the thinking-mode guide requires it on later requests that carry tools; the API tolerated the omission, so nothing failed visibly.
impact: Every new user message (Ask confirmation, nudge) dropped the prefix cache back to the previous user message: 30-40% of cache misses in recorded v1.9.1 sessions, and the model lost its own reasoning between tool steps. Paired off-peak check (user-approved, about CNY 0.03): miss 3,515 tokens without pass-back vs 221 with it on the same new-user request.
lesson: Check provider protocol requirements against the request actually sent; a tolerant API is not evidence of a correct request.

cause: Routing overrides auto-detected panel columns only for the column the user or Agent supplied; with entity_col set and time_col unset, the auto-detected time column (year) still reaches PanelOLS, which adds TimeEffects.
impact: A firm-only fixed-effects request on data with a detectable time column is fitted as two-way FE: in the paid pass-back round the firm-only and firm+year fits were byte-identical (df_model 210), the isolated reviewer blocked completion 12 times (~CNY 0.38) and the task ran out of nudges.
lesson: An explicitly declared specification must not be completed from auto-detection; when any panel column is declared, an undeclared one means no effect.

cause: I sized the per-mode caps from expected spend; the ledger reserves each request's worst case from body bytes (about CNY 1.33 at peak prices with reasoning pass-back), so the Ask cap stopped panel_fe mid-task and the Auto pass was stopped by hand.
impact: About CNY 0.3 bought one partial task; the round was rerun with one shared ledger and finished within the user's CNY 2 (total CNY 1.05).
lesson: Size a paid round's cap as expected spend plus one worst-case request reservation.

cause: Routing overrides auto-detected panel columns only for the column the user or Agent supplied; with entity_col set and time_col unset, the auto-detected time column (year) still reaches PanelOLS, which adds TimeEffects.
impact: A firm-only fixed-effects request on data with a detectable time column is fitted as two-way FE: in the paid pass-back round the firm-only and firm+year fits were byte-identical (df_model 210), the isolated reviewer blocked completion 12 times (~CNY 0.38) and the task ran out of nudges. Rerun values change for entity-only specifications; recorded in the v1.9.1 release-notes draft.

cause: The review parser accepts an evidence_ref only when it equals a packet key; the reviewer cites paths inside keys (plan.criteria[2], diagnostic:0.summary...).
impact: In the recorded Auto loop 6 of 10 reviews were discarded as inconsistent_verdict_or_unknown_evidence_reference, including the finding that exposed the panel time-effects bug; a path-aware check would accept 4 of them. Awaiting the user's decision.
lesson: Validate model citations by what they point to, not by exact spelling, and keep refusing references outside the supplied evidence.

cause: User decided (2026-10-22) to hand back an earlier blocking review instead of calling the reviewer again when the verified evidence is unchanged.
impact: Implemented across commands only: within one command the designed revision and recheck stay, because a strict same-evidence reuse would make wording-level blocking findings unfixable (existing test test_auto_uses_critique_to_revise_once_then_rechecks). On the recorded Auto loop this cuts reviews from 10 to 3.
lesson: When a user rule conflicts with a tested design case, implement the rule where it does not break the case and report the boundary.

cause: The review parser accepts an evidence_ref only when it equals a packet key; the reviewer cites paths inside keys (plan.criteria[2], diagnostic:0.summary...).

cause: Loopback transport was treated as proof of local inference even when a gateway forwarded requests to a cloud provider.
impact: Cloud gateway requests could receive local content-class and sensitive-column privileges. Explicit processing location now controls sends, reviewer preflight, UI and audit; historical data exposure is not assessed.
lesson: Separate the transport endpoint from the final data-processing boundary. Unknown and historical configurations receive remote protection; invalid configurations must not select another provider.

cause: The user connected a free DeepSeek route (Magpie -> WorkBuddy, workbuddy-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash) and authorised free calls.
impact: Probe: ~2 s first token, 100-200 tok/s, 210k context, cache reported, credit 0; the route answers without thinking unless reasoning_effort is sent. V4 is now recognised by model id and requests state reasoning_effort=high (the official default); eval runs use a free-route guard that stops on any non-zero credit. Whether M5 may count results from this route is the user's decision (baseline was the official API).
lesson: A gateway serving the same model id can differ in defaults; probe thinking, cache and usage before trusting it.

cause: c11a1a6d stopped adding time effects for entity-only panel fits but also dropped the time index, so panel diagnostics saw n_times = nobs and no time pairing.
impact: The free-route Auto panel task was blocked by the reviewer on this until its nudges ran out. Fixed: time indexes the fit and its diagnostics; effects follow the declaration.
lesson: Separate a model's effects from the data's structure; a fix to one must keep the other.

cause: Free-route round: 35 refused tool calls in 8 tasks and 7 review-driven nudges in one task, mostly identity the backend binds, read tools given a branch head, hidden PlanValidationError reasons and reviewer citations by evidence identity.
impact: Agent-facing targets need only run_id/node_ref; unused identity is dropped with workbench_notes; derived-run reads resolve under the head; PlanValidationError reasons are visible; reviewer citations may name packet identities. Offline: 12 of 35 refused calls now pass; survival reviews accepted 5 of 8 (was 1). Remaining refusals are real analysis/spec errors.
lesson: When the backend owns a fact, never make the model supply it; absorb, verify and report instead of refusing.

cause: The leverage scenario scored estimates against the population slope 1.0, but the goal variant's fixed draw supports 1.276 on its clean rows, so no correct analysis could pass.
impact: User-approved grader v2 (2026-10-22): scenarios may declare a sample truth (leverage: OLS on the generator's clean rows); v1 keeps the frozen behaviour. Recompute over 19 rounds / 187 tasks: v1 equals the frozen grader on every task; v2 changes only leverage tasks; baseline outcomes unchanged; 5 candidate leverage.goal runs become recovered. Both versions are reported.
lesson: Score a simulated task against what its fixed draw supports, and check every fixed seed's oracle before freezing a grader.

cause: In the no-thinking round the weaker model miscopied a 64-hex source sha256 (one digit) and named a report that did not cover the selected results; the gate refused without saying what was wrong.
impact: 3 of 8 no-thinking tasks used all nudges (iv_weak Ask, panel_fe Auto, survival Auto). The source sha256 is now bound by the server, a non-covering named report is returned with what it lacks and the covering report or compose_report, and a single string for a list of strings is wrapped.
lesson: Every value the server can determine must be bound by the server; a model should only make choices.

cause: c49d247b expressed no thinking as a reasoning_effort of none beside a disabled thinking switch; the Magpie gateway thinks whenever the reasoning_effort field is present, whatever its value.
impact: The bounded planner and report-writer config thought within its 8192 output limit on the free route, and the first none round thought on 17 of 20 calls, so it was not the weak-floor measurement. No thinking is now expressed only by the disabled thinking switch; a true no-thinking round was run.
lesson: Probe each gateway control value, including combinations, before relying on it.

cause: operation.multi_step proposals targeting a model node were admitted; workflow compilation at confirmation requires a dataset node and raised an unmapped validation error (HTTP 500), leaving the record pending.
impact: Free-route off3 leverage.goal (Ask, no thinking): six confirmations never ran, including three report compositions, while the Agent was told each had run; the task ended on the nudge budget.
lesson: An admitted proposal must be executable: resolve the source node when the proposal is made, and fail the operation record (not the server) when it stops resolving.

cause: The completion gate named a missing distinct-point-estimation or influence-sample comparison but gave no executable next step, and its next_step asked for the report first.
impact: Free-route off3 (no thinking): iv_weak.goal and leverage.goal ended on the nudge budget; the leverage report was composed before the fit it lacked. After adding validated options from the primary's own specification, offline replay reached requirements_met with the influence refit recovering the clean-row slope (1.2764 for 1.276).
lesson: Every requirement the gate reports as missing needs an executable next step derived from server-known facts; ordering matters when a later product must cover an earlier one.

cause: Continuations set the command text to None, so language detection fell back to English, and publication prepended a notice to answers that already began with one.
impact: Chinese tasks showed stacked English and Chinese partial notices in off3 answers.
lesson: A continuation inherits the person's last request; published notices replace, not stack.

cause: The free-route guard only judged usage.credit: a gateway that could not be reached was retried by the product, and a 429 rate limit was reported as missing credit.
impact: Round off4 was void (its first task spent all nudges in seconds on ConnectError); off4b's Auto mode stopped after one task with a misleading reason, and the route is limited until 2026-10-23 20:56 UTC+8.
lesson: A round guard must name every way a provider can refuse service and stop on the first one that makes further tasks meaningless.

cause: The free-route guard tolerated three transport interruptions per round; WorkBuddy Hy3 and Step-5-Preview sometimes send no first byte for 90 s on 160-430 KB requests, which the product correctly abandons.
impact: The first new-model round voided 15 of 16 tasks: Hy3 stopped half-way through its first task, Step-5 after two completed tasks (both correct, 3-5x slower than DeepSeek without thinking).
lesson: Bound provider interruptions where they happen (per task) and end only that task; a round-level count turns one slow task into a missing round.

cause: With models other than DeepSeek on the free route, a no-progress stall ended the turn: 26 of 92 Hy3 turns and 22 of 54 Step-5 turns needed the person to say continue. The user set the goal that the Agent succeed with any model and approved a bounded retry.
impact: The v1.8.5 rule is refined, not dropped: a stalled stream is still abandoned at the idle bound and never waited on; a fresh request follows after 5 s then 15 s, at most twice per turn, never after visible output; Stop interrupts the wait.
lesson: Separate abandoning a stalled stream (always) from asking again with a fresh request (bounded per turn); provider reliability differs by model and route.

cause: The evaluation recorder read each streamed reply whole before passing it on, so the product's 90 s no-progress bound measured total generation time; answers longer than 90 s were cut. I attributed the resulting Hy3 and Step-5 'stalls' to the WorkBuddy route and changed the guard and retry policy around them.
impact: Hy3 and Step-5 rounds understated both models (failed and slow tasks, 26/92 and 22/54 turns ending on a cut); a verification round was stopped once the 90 s ceiling (no successful call above it across 600+ calls) and a direct streaming probe (first chunk at 1.6 s) exposed the cause.
lesson: When a failure has a sharp ceiling equal to one of our own bounds, check the harness path end to end (probe without it) before blaming the provider.

User decision 2026-10-25: keep the statistical rule (Cook's distance above the diagnostic's own threshold), name rows by zero-based position via data.subset exclude_row_indices when no ID column exists, and turn the requirement into a report disclosure only when the data itself rules the refit out.

lesson: Every evaluation script pins the model it means to measure and checks the first request's model before trusting the round.

lesson: Keep gateway refusal and unknown billing distinct from statistical failure. Stopped free-route ledgers require explicit resolution, not storage exceptions or unapproved alternate-model attempts.

cause: Baseline-only whole-worker RSS variation was 5.273364 percent in five calibrations, exceeding the unchanged less-than-five-percent requirement. The observed paired medians therefore do not certify native acceleration.
lesson: Keep calibration failures and raw observations even when candidate medians look better; component measurements do not certify default-path end-to-end performance.

cause: The shared request builder encoded every declared none effort as DeepSeek thinking disabled. The NVIDIA documented standard reasoning_effort none was absent in the captured request; the new regression test failed before the minimal correction.
lesson: Keep provider-specific reasoning controls behind their provider/model boundary; configure explicit supported efforts and verify the actual bounded tool request with mocks before live access.

cause: The agent-created backend preview lacked the configured frontend5195 origin, so the real browser proxy could read without an Origin header in the earlier check but refused browser-origin requests. The provider dropdown also lacked an NVIDIA preset.
lesson: Check the actual frontend proxy with browser Origin and a no-op save before handing off credential setup; configure the preview origin explicitly instead of weakening the request guard.

cause: DeepSeekV4.1Flash and GLM5.3Flash each received one authorized request attempt but produced no HTTP response within60seconds. Usage and the provider-side cause remain unknown; neither was retried.
lesson: Separate once-per-model transport/tool smoke from complete Agent evaluation; retain no-response and unknown usage without inferring unsupported tools or zero cost, and do not turn another explicitly authorized model probe into an invisible fallback.

cause: Provider cards cached the on-mount snapshot and retained a model-specific provider name. That local UI issue is fixed. Separately, two NVIDIA endpoints still returned no response headers after complete TLS/request send, including minimal requests without tools; remote processing or return-path cause is unresolved.
lesson: Reload local provider state without remote calls; diagnose timeout phase with a minimal no-tool control before changing tool code. Mark unanswered remote endpoints unverified and retain accounting uncertainty rather than looping or claiming success.

cause: NVIDIA configured waits were truncated independently by HTTP silence30s and Agent idle90s; timeout alone does not identify remote availability or congestion.
lesson: Use one provider waiting policy across transport and Agent, preserve explicit overrides and independent abort; distinguish documented free entitlement, model-card limits, hosted limits and observed runtime outcomes.

cause: Model mappings used intrinsic-minimum fractional columns and unconstrained preformatted JSON; model ID was also part of the React row key, remounting focused inputs on edits. Plain model labels became unreadable with18 entries; initial large tiles were rejected for low density.
lesson: Constrain min-content at grid/container/input boundaries, keep editable values out of React identity keys, and verify dense real catalogs plus expanded previews in a browser; model window caps must not exceed declared capacity.

cause: The review projection discarded real correlation/group lists yet claimed completeness; rerun declaration preflight swallowed unavailable source inputs before proposal admission. Both allowed a misleading success/readiness signal.
lesson: Review packets must retain needed producer aggregates or declare incomplete; unreadable evidence is an actionable refusal before human confirmation, never an empty success. Preserve editable-target early rejection and original failures; scoped fake-model evidence is not live accuracy.

cause: Independent review checked whether sibling reruns invalidated their source head, and reproduced observer polling after unmount while an authorized operation remained running.
lesson: A selected group is presentation, not new authority: confirm each immutable revision/source, stop future confirmations and polling on cancellation/unmount, preserve actual receipts and resume once. Prove sibling chain semantics with real stores rather than an invalid two-head mock.

cause: Replacing a partial budget erased other approved caps; explicit narrower or empty permission classes were ignored. Finite steps changed to accepted zero meant unlimited without reopening approval.
lesson: Treat plan budgets as patches; distinguish omitted restrictions from explicit empty ones. Preserve the established zero-as-unlimited contract but require human reapproval for expansion. Test real Auto admission after updates, not only serialized plan values; no-op parameter validators or unrelated durations cannot certify L1 feasibility or execution estimates.

cause: Automatic approval review rejected launching the user-requested fixed-eight evaluation because explicit permission of the named benchmark data transfer to NVIDIA Ultra was required. A single bundled data-egress question is pending; no inference was made and no execution workaround was used.
lesson: Separate concrete evaluation intent from the automatic reviewer's explicit data-and-recipient egress approval requirement; preserve a reviewable frozen candidate and viewer while awaiting approval, never reroute a rejected launch.

cause: User explicitly permitted both evaluation batches named data transfer, resolving prior egress approval gate. The first IV Ask request streamed public content and a tool request; local finish_reason handling closed the response before final usage, so the recorder retained CancelledError and stopped the round. This is not provider unavailability.
lesson: For the exact Ultra route, request final usage accounting and read the bounded completion tail before exposing tools or done. Retain true interruption failures and original unknown usage; offline synthetic tail replay cannot reconcile an abandoned live request. Other NVIDIA models retain their prior protocol.

cause: User approved preserving the first unknown attempt and starting the repaired candidate. IV Ask exhausted eight nudges with no IV model and eight of fifteen tools refused. Panel Ask later received a complete SSE error frame with provider code503 and no usage; early error-path close was taped as CancelledError. No retry or later task was started.
lesson: Distinguish an observed analysis failure from provider overload and preserve every failed attempt. An SSE error inside HTTP200 must be recognized before local close cancellation masks its cause; never treat missing usage as zero or silently retry. Frozen graders lacking NVIDIA cache fields cannot certify zero cache hits.

cause: The user explicitly approved complete503 overload errors without any generated output as the only unknown-usage retry exception:60/120 seconds, at most two retries per request, ten shared across dev8 and QRData40. Retain IV Ask failure and old ledgers; restart panel in a fresh project then the remaining six fixed tasks and original QR40.
lesson: Opt-in recovery belongs in the evaluation harness: persist global and per-request counts, preserve original payloads and every error tape, keep unknown usage out of settled charges, and stop on other failures, cancellation or unresolved restart tickets. Offline recovery checks do not prove live quality.

cause: The resumed fixed panel task produced three non-seed model artifacts, then its37th exchange raised ReadError before response headers after46.867 seconds. No response bytes or usage were received. This is outside the permitted complete503-only recovery and the guard correctly stopped. Offline IV recording also exposed general contract/feedback gaps; those are repaired without changing the frozen live product.
lesson: Do not widen a named503 exception into general unknown-usage recovery. Preserve partial work and distinguish raw tape accounting from frozen grader placeholders for interrupted tasks. General type/contract/reference feedback repairs require independent offline checks and cannot retroactively improve retained real results.
